algorithm: Odd. |x| < 2^-12 returns x, which is the correctly rounded tanh: |x - tanh(x)| < x^3/3 is below half an ulp on that range. |x| >= 9.01091385 (bits 0x41102cb4) returns ±1, the correctly rounded value. In between, slot i of width 2^-14 holds an f32 anchor tanh(i/16384) and an f32 slope across the slot. The value is anchor + slope * (x - i/16384), each mul and add rounded on its own. black_box on the CPU, det_bar in WGSL. The table is crates/ferric-core/src/det_tanh_table.bin, generated by scripts/fit_det_tanh.py.

argmax_note: Smallest positive bit pattern whose result is 1 ulp from correctly rounded tanh. Many larger inputs are also 1 ulp. None are 2 or more.
non_correctly_rounded_note: Both signs. Sign symmetry held on every finite input, so 28278900 per sign.
midpoint_note: Positive inputs whose f64 tanh fell within 1e-12 of an f32 midpoint. Those were recomputed with a 20-term double-double exp and then rounded to f32. The negative side uses the sign flip of that decision.

coverage.finite_note: Every finite f32, both signs, including ±0 and every subnormal. 2^32 - 2^24.

shader.includes: ±0, ±inf, a NaN payload, subnormals, the saturation edge, and a stride across [0, sat)

generator_note: numpy.tanh on Ubuntu 24.04 (numpy 1.26.4, glibc 2.39) rebuilds the committed bytes. Rust f64::tanh does not: it disagrees at f32 rounding on 17977 of the 295270 stored words. The bit-exact generator is the Python script, not f64::tanh.
